chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Jess, a younger dancer from Homestead
summary: Jess was a couple of years younger and worked as a dancer; she lost touch with him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Can you tell us something a little bit more about him? He worked in Pittsburgh?

Yeah, well he was younger -- Jess was a couple years younger than I was and he had started out quite early to dance and he played the guitar, too. I think on some occasions he played with Harry. And when Harry would work in clubs I think Jess would probably perform on the job.

See, I couldn't get into the clubs because my voice was too soft and the clubs that Harry worked in, this was before microphones and I just couldn't be heard and the singers he had there was these robust women who could sing in the middle of Yankee Stadium and you could hear them in the last row. But Jess worked around quite a bit. He became popular. He left Homestead early and he went out -- I think he went to Detroit and he teamed up with another young man and they used to play guitars and sing and dance.

I don't know where Jess is now. I don't know whether he's still living or not. The last

That was in Detroit you saw him last?
But up until that time, he'd actually been working as a dancer?

Oh, yes. Yes. I don't recall that he made it in the so-called Big Time, but I know that he worked around -- he danced for a living for quite a few years. And of course, I lost track of him, his being in Detroit and my being in New York. I really didn't keep up with his career. We didn't correspond or anything like that.
